validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION + SPEC all confirmed HIGH. IGAT 7 (Seventh Iran Gas Trunkline) is a real, operating 56-in gas TRANSMISSION trunk from Asalouyeh (Persian Gulf) to Iranshahr in Sistan-Baluchistan, carrying South Pars gas. Oil & Gas Journal (13 Sep 2010, independent) states verbatim: '907-km, 56-in. OD Iran Gas Trunkline 7 (IGAT 7) from Asalouyeh ... to Iranshahr', capacity '1.8 bcfd' (expandable to 2.9 bcfd), operator 'National Iranian Gas Co.', gas flow began 'Aug. 23' 2010, source 'South Pars offshore gas field'. offshore-technology market page independently confirms 56-in and 1.8 bcfd. Persian source naftema.com independently gives the route عسلویه-سرخون-ایرانشهر (Asaluyeh-Sarkhoon-Iranshahr), 56-in, and 902 km, and attributes trunkline operation to شرکت ملی گاز ایران (NIGC). GEM values match: Status=operating OK, PipelineType=transmission OK, Fuel=Gas OK, Diameter=56 in OK, Capacity=1800 MMcf/d = 1.8 bcfd OK, StartYear1=2010 OK, FuelSource=South Pars OK, endpoints Asaluyeh(Bushehr)->Iranshahr(Sistan-Baluchistan) OK. Minor SPEC caveat: length 907 km (OGJ) vs 902 km (naftema / some NIGC figures) — a rounding/measurement variant of the same trunk, not a material conflict; keep 907 with OGJ ref. The sheet's own existing Status and Length ref (offshore-technology teaser) does not surface those specific values (verifier FAILs on '907' and 'operating') — replace with OGJ.

validity.researcher_notes: NAME COLLISION / segment double-count risk. Row P2015 (sheet_row 2387) carries the IDENTICAL name 'IGAT 7 Gas Pipeline' but different specs: LengthKnown=290 km, Capacity=1100 MMcf/d, StartYear1=2024, ShelvedYear=2012, Owner=National Iranian Gas Co, endpoints only 'Iran'->'Iran'. P0446 is the well-documented 907 km / 1.8 bcfd main trunk (Asaluyeh->Iranshahr, operating 2010). P2015's ~290 km with a 2024 start most plausibly represents the Iranshahr->Iran/Pakistan-border extension (OGJ notes a '270-kilometre part from Iranshahr to the Iran-Pakistan border') or a downstream Sistan-Baluchistan spur, i.e. a DIFFERENT physical segment of the IGAT-7 system rather than the same pipe. So P0446 is NOT itself a phantom or a full duplicate — but the shared exact name across two rows is a data-hygiene defect that risks double-counting the IGAT-7 trunk. P0446 should be retained as the canonical main trunk; P2015 needs a human decision (distinct-segment relabel vs fold-in). Named the other PID: P2015.

routes.corridor_desc: Eastbound coastal/near-coastal corridor along the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman hinterland: from the Asalouyeh/South Pars complex in Bushehr Province, the line runs southeast through Hormozgan Province via the Sarkhoon gas refinery near Bandar Abbas, then east-northeast into Sistan-Baluchistan Province to Iranshahr. Persian source explicitly gives the corridor as Asaluyeh-Sarkhoon-Iranshahr. Endpoints and the Sarkhoon waypoint are well sourced; the exact intermediate alignment across Hormozgan/Sistan-Baluchistan is inferred from the named waypoints (tight enough to bound to the coastal corridor, not a meter-level trace).
